segments.text: This is the first and only time
astronomers have detected an atmosphere
on an Earth-like planet in the habitable
zone. It's 49 light-years away and it's
leaking helium and there could be liquid
water on the surface. This is a huge
deal because this star is much dimmer
and smaller than our Sun, which means
the habitable zone is right up next to
it. So, a year on this planet is only 25
days for us. But, being that close,
you've got two big issues. One, planets
that close are tidally locked like our
moon, meaning one side is always in
darkness and the other is always facing
the star. This planet is tidally locked,
meaning the surface might look like a
weird eyeball, super icy with an ocean
at the center. The second problem is
radiation because typically the
atmospheres of planets that are this
close get ripped away by radiation from
their star and without that, life as we
know it can't exist. But, not here. The
detection of helium means that this
planet has an atmosphere even though the
upper part is slowly evaporating [music]
into space. But, this planet is over
five times more massive than Earth. So,
scientists think that it could be
holding on to a thicker atmosphere
closer to the surface and the James Webb
Space Telescope is learning more. So, to
see it, subscribe.
